---
title: "Moving or renaming a renv project can break its library"
ref: RNV-06
categories: [renv and installation]
impact: cryptique
attendu: "the same project, with the same packages, in its new location"
versions: "All versions of {renv}"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2021)"
---

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```bash
mv ~/projects/analysis ~/projects/analysis-2021
cd ~/projects/analysis-2021
Rscript -e 'library(dplyr)'
```
:::

This pitfall depends on the file system and the {renv} cache, so it cannot be replayed in the browser.

## Why

The library of a {renv} project does not really contain the packages: they are links to the global {renv} cache. Depending on the system and on how the folder is moved (copy, archive, file sync, another drive), those links can be lost or point to nothing.

When the library is stored outside the project (the `RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY_ROOT` variable), its location also depends on the project's name and path: after a rename, {renv} looks for another library, an empty one. Either way, the errors talk about packages that cannot be found, not about the move.

## The remedy

Do not rely on the library after a move: rebuild it from the lockfile, which is all it takes to describe the project.

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```r
renv::restore()
renv::status()
```
:::
